issues.body: `has_only_iri_chars` repairs percent escapes and code-point ranges, but the function explicitly does not enforce component structure even though `is_absolute_iri` is documented and consumed as an absolute-IRI predicate. For example, strings such as `http://[` or `http://example.com:bad-port` contain a valid scheme and only admitted characters, so this predicate accepts them despite invalid authority/host/port syntax. Used by expansion step 15.4, that still permits invalid datatype IRIs to avoid `InvalidTypedValue`. This is materially the round-one finding: one cited witness is fixed, but the general RFC 3987 validation obligation is not.
issues.fix_hint: Use a standards-complete RFC 3987 IRI parser/validator for this predicate, or implement the complete `IRI = scheme ':' ihier-part [ '?' iquery ] [ '#' ifragment ]` grammar including authority, host/IP-literal, port, path, query, fragment, and `iprivate` placement. Add end-to-end datatype negative tests for structurally invalid strings that use only otherwise legal characters, plus positive tests for representative authority-less schemes and Unicode IRIs.
issues.title: Datatype validation still omits RFC 3987 structural syntax

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes the malformed-percent and Unicode code-point cases identified in round 1, and adds useful non-vacuous regression tests. However, the same major correctness issue remains at a narrower boundary: `is_absolute_iri` still claims to recognize an absolute RFC 3987 IRI and is used to satisfy JSON-LD expansion's datatype-IRI validation obligation, while the implementation explicitly omits the RFC 3987 structural grammar. It therefore accepts invalid absolute-looking strings composed only of admitted characters. Because invalid datatype IRIs can still expand successfully, the change remains incomplete and cannot be approved.
